title: A release's own body claims it fixed an issue that's still open
author: off-by-one
description: Extracts every real GitHub closing keyword (fixes/closes/resolves #N, both tenses, tools/closing_keyword_guard.py's own grammar) from a release's body text and checks the named issue's real state. An issue that exists but is still open is the seam: the release is a permanent public record claiming a fix that, in fact, never landed.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the release published, mirroring release-claims-unmerged-pr's own reasoning: a claim checked within a few hours of publish might still be a race (release published moments before the real fix lands) rather than a settled documentation error (0.5, below the 0.70 bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden); a full day or more past publish with the named issue still open is unambiguous (flat 0.85, the release body is static once published). A named issue that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0 -- that broken reference is dangling-issue-reference's own seam, not this one's. A named issue that IS closed is excluded too, named not hidden -- the claim was true.
